thread:
Cassie H: Hey team - stayed at an Airbnb for a client visit last week. Company card was used for the booking but host charged an extra $150 cleaning fee after checkout and also placed a $300 security deposit hold that hasn't released (4 days later). The booking folio only showed $120 cleaning at booking. How do I get the company card charge reconciled?
Jordan (People Ops): Sorry that happened. Does the host invoice show reason for extra cleaning? And was the $300 a pre-authorization or an actual charge?
Cassie H: Host sent a message saying "deep cleaning fee applied" and attached a photo of a broken glass in the living room. The $300 shows as a pending authorization on the company card (appears as Airbnb *HostXYZ) not a posted charge yet. Photo of glass is small and looks like a hairline chip. I didn't sign anything.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: Damage claims by hosts are handled case-by-case. If company card is charged, Finance requires (1) host invoice with line-item detail, (2) host photos, (3) host's refund policy link, and (4) manager approval to dispute or accept charges. Pending authorizations are monitored; Finance will only reimburse posted charges.
Liam - Ops: Cassie, was the team desk notified? If the company card is used, we prefer Travel Desk to coordinate disputes so Travel/Finance handles vendor communications. Did you notify travel@redwood.com?
Cassie H: I messaged the host and travel@redwood.com just now. Host said charge is final and deposit will be released in 7-14 days depending on their process. Manager (Priya) says we should dispute if it's unreasonable. Priya added a quick note approving dispute on the expense thread.
Jordan (People Ops): Ok please upload: host message, photo of damage, original booking folio showing $120 cleaning, company card transaction screenshot showing pending $300 auth, and manager note "Priya approves dispute". Tag expense as "airbnb-deposit-dispute".
Cassie H: Uploaded all docs to the report. I left a comment in the expense: "Host post-charge $150 cleaning + $300 auth on company card; manager approves dispute."
Host Support Bot: Automatic note: Airbnb resolution center suggests contacting the host first. If unresolved, open a claim within 72 hours of checkout and supply evidence. For company cards, please instruct Finance to wait for host response before issuing reimbursement.
Finance Bot: Received attachments. Next steps: 1) Finance will hold reimbursement while dispute in progress. 2) If host posts the $300 as a charge and it is later reversed, Finance will reconcile. 3) If host provides an itemized invoice that Finance deems unreasonable, we'll escalate to Airbnb resolution and require a written manager sign-off to escalate payment if necessary.
Liam - Ops: If host refuses to refund and the charge posts, do we absorb or require host to refund? We should aim to recover from host or Airbnb. Ops happy to assist with escalation if Travel Desk needs it.
Jordan (People Ops): For policy clarity: company will not reimburse questionable damage claims without manager sign-off and sufficient evidence. If the charge is legitimate (clearly documented damage) company will reimburse. If rejected, employee won't be on the hook because company card was used. We'll attempt recovery from host/Airbnb.
Cassie H: Thanks. ETA on Finance actions? I'm blocked from closing my expense.
Finance Bot: Manual review started. We'll monitor the pending auth. If the $300 posts, Finance will pause auto-reimbursement and open a recovery case. Expected update within 5 business days or when host replies. We'll notify here.
Jordan (People Ops): Thanks for flagging it early, Cassie. If host posts unreasonable claims, please ping me and I'll coordinate manager escalation.
Cassie H: Got it. I'll keep an eye and add any new host messages here. Appreciate the quick help :pray:
